Definition: feminine of the ordinal of G4004; fiftieth (G2250 being implied) from Passover, i.e. the festival of "Pentecost":--Pentecost.
BiblicalUsage: Pentekoste is the fiftieth day, the feast of Pentecost. When the day of Pentecost was fully come, the disciples were all with one accord in one place, and the Spirit came. Paul hasted to be at Jerusalem for the day of Pentecost, and he tarried at Ephesus until Pentecost.
TheologicalSignificance: I am convinced that Pentecost is the birthday of the church: the Spirit came, the disciples spoke, and three thousand were added. I hold that the feast that once marked the harvest now marks the harvest of souls, and the same Spirit who fell then still falls on those who wait in one accord. The fiftieth day is not a date on a calendar to me — it is the day God kept His promise.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
